(v)~At a representative growth $\alpha=0.1$, the constrained growth-induced stress is
reproduced to within $0.1\%$ by a \emph{second, independently coded} routine: an
alternative UMAT built on a neo-Hookean rather than a Hencky elastic potential, but
sharing the same isotropic growth split $\bF_{\!g}=(1+\alpha)\bI$. The agreement confirms
that the \emph{growth-kinematics implementation} carries no code-specific artefact; the
two elastic potentials necessarily diverge at larger strain, so the check is a moderate-
strain implementation cross-check rather than a constitutive-equivalence claim.
